items.rationale: Sections 2.3.2 and 7.1.7(b) cover a like-for-like frame for the theft-damaged bicycle, with fitting priced separately. The €3,500 agreed value replaces the €500 mobility cap under 4.4; the estimated repair and recovery costs do not exhaust it.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 cover brakes equivalent to those damaged in the theft, not an upgrade. The estimate is for one gross parts line, with fitting priced separately.

Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary freight for replacement parts or the bicycle, but 7.1.8(g) excludes any transport already billed elsewhere. Allow €25 for one ordinary shipment if documented as distinct.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f) cover a necessary repair attendance, but the account does not establish a separate bicycle-service visit. Allow €39 for one necessary trip if it is distinct from shipping and the locksmith call-out.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fitting, alignment and testing after frame and brake replacement. Allow €180 for the assembly work, excluding any work already billed in the hourly lines under 7.1.8(g).
Section 7.1.7(e) covers small fixings and consumables actually used in the repair, not shop overhead. Allow €12 for one modest sundries line.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers necessary apprentice labour stated separately by grade. Allow one hour at €35.50 gross if the work is not already included in assembly.
Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.8(g) allow separately identifiable skilled repair work, but not double billing of assembly. Allow one distinct hour at €65 gross.
The locksmith had to attend the recovery scene, so the trip is covered under 5.2.2(a). Allow €39 gross for one call-out, consistent with the closest reference; the €1,000 recovery cap does not bind.

The recovery context supports treating this flat charge as cutting and releasing the seized lock under 5.2.2(b), not fitting a new lock. Allow €105 gross, provided it does not duplicate the separately billed labour.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers materials consumed in releasing the lock, while 7.1.8(d) excludes the trade's own tools and equipment. Allow €7 gross if the sundries are shown to be specific to the release.
Section 5.2.2(b) expressly covers labour of every grade used in the release. Allow one apprentice hour at €35.50 gross, consistent with the closest reference, if separately incurred.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled release labour, but 7.1.8(g) bars payment for the same work twice. Allow €42 gross for one separately justified hour, calibrated to the comparable charge below €45.
